BL-1348 — The vitest worker pool reserves 1280 MB a fork against a measured 298 MB peak, so an explicit operator fork override is silently clamped to seven and fourteen of twenty cores idle through every property run
What it solves: ## Every intake measurement re-verified at mint, none taken on trust
Approval context: Your directive, verbatim, is preserved in source: below. Nothing here is broken and nothing is at risk either way - the pool is behaving exactly as BL-422 designed it after the 13 GB OOM incident, on a RAM model that has simply never been re-measured. The whole ticket is a missed opportunity to use…
BL-1348 needs your approval before it can proceed. Reply here with "approve BL-1348" (or "reject BL-1348 <reason>") to act.
